verdict.rationale: a-Shell's main programmatic interface is its own set of documented Apple Shortcuts actions: `Execute Command` runs a list of commands in order, and `Put File`/`Get File` move files in and out, so Shortcuts can drive the shell. This is not a general public API: there is no HTTP/REST, SDK or OpenAPI spec (the probes for llms.txt and OpenAPI returned 404), and the docs warn that forcing a shortcut to run in App or in Extension 'won't always work'. missing for 10: a documented general-purpose public API (REST/SDK/OpenAPI), API reference docs beyond the Shortcuts action descriptions, independent corroboration of agent-driven use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: a-Shell is compatible with Apple Shortcuts, giving users full control of the Shell.
`Execute Command`, which takes a list of commands and executes them in order. The input can also be a file or a text node
`Put File` and `Get File` are used to transfer files to and from a-Shell.
